ambiguities.evidence: The paper uses scalar absolute values and the real-valued sign expression sign(ell_j(x)) in the maximizing perturbation, but does not state a formal real-scalar type. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: proof of Lemma 2.2.)
ambiguities.impact: A formal contract should not silently generalize the stated maximizing perturbation to complex scalars; a complex version would require phases rather than the displayed sign choice.
ambiguities.issue: The scalar field is not explicitly declared in the selected setup. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Section 2 and proof of Lemma 2.2.)

ambiguities.evidence: Epsilon multiplies nonnegative componentwise magnitudes and acts as a perturbation radius, making approach through positive values the natural reading, but that direction is not printed separately. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Definition 2.1.)
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must make the conventional positive-radius interpretation explicit.
ambiguities.issue: Definition 2.1 writes epsilon -> 0 without explicitly stating a one-sided limit or epsilon >= 0. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Definition 2.1.)

contract_plain_english: For fixed distinct nodes and a fixed evaluation point, the exact interpolant's componentwise relative condition number with respect to its n+1 data values is the sum of |ell_j(x)f_j| divided by |p_n(x)|, and this number is at least one; the result applies only when p_n(x) is nonzero. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Section 2, Definition 2.1, and Lemma 2.2 equation (2.2).)

source_evidence.observation: The paper fixes distinct interpolation points x_j indexed by j=0,...,n and an evaluation point x, varies the data vector f, writes the degree-at-most-n interpolant as p_f(x)=p_n(x), and defines p_n(x)=sum_{j=0}^n f_j ell_j(x) with the displayed Lagrange basis.

For p_n(x) != 0, the condition number is defined by a limit as epsilon tends to zero of the supremum of the relative output change divided by epsilon, subject to the componentwise relative perturbation condition |Delta f| <= epsilon |f|.
The lemma explicitly gives cond(x,n,f)=sum_{j=0}^n |ell_j(x)f_j|/|p_n(x)| and explicitly asserts that this quantity is at least 1.
The proof derives the numerator from linear dependence on Delta f and states that equality in the maximizing bound is attained by choosing Delta f_j=epsilon sign(ell_j(x))|f_j|.

statement.algorithm_linkage: No evaluation algorithm or floating-point implementation is selected: Lemma 2.2 conditions the exact Lagrange interpolation value with respect to data perturbations at fixed nodes and fixed x. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Section 2 and Lemma 2.2.)
binders: An interpolation parameter n, n+1 scalar data values f_j, and n+1 distinct scalar interpolation points x_j indexed by j=0,...,n are in scope. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Section 2 opening paragraph.)
The interpolation points x_j and evaluation point x are fixed, while the data vector f varies; p_f(x) is another name for p_n(x). (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Section 2 opening paragraph.)
Definition 2.1 binds componentwise perturbations Delta f and a perturbation radius epsilon in the limit epsilon -> 0. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Definition 2.1.)
conclusions: cond(x,n,f) = [sum_{j=0}^n |ell_j(x) f_j|]/|p_n(x)|. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Lemma 2.2, equation (2.2).)
cond(x,n,f) >= 1. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Lemma 2.2, equation (2.2).)

The proof identifies a maximizing perturbation by Delta f_j=epsilon sign(ell_j(x))|f_j|, establishing equality with the closed-form upper bound. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: proof of Lemma 2.2.)
constants_and_indexing: Every sum in equation (2.2) runs from j=0 through j=n and therefore contains n+1 terms. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Lemma 2.2, equation (2.2).)
The lower-bound constant is exactly 1. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Lemma 2.2, equation (2.2).)
definitions_and_conventions: p_n(x)=sum_{j=0}^n f_j ell_j(x), where ell_j(x)=[product over k=0,...,n, k != j of (x-x_k)]/[product over k=0,...,n, k != j of (x_j-x_k)]. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: equation (2.1).)
cond(x,n,f)=lim_{epsilon->0} sup { |p_f(x)-p_{f+Delta f}(x)|/[epsilon |p_f(x)|] : |Delta f| <= epsilon |f| }. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Definition 2.1.)
Inequalities and absolute values applied to vectors are interpreted componentwise. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Section 2 opening paragraph.)
The argument n in cond(x,n,f) records dependence on the interpolation points x_j. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: paragraph following Definition 2.1.)
error_notions: The input error notion is componentwise relative perturbation: |Delta f_j| <= epsilon |f_j| for every j. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Definition 2.1.)
The output error notion is the relative scalar change |p_f(x)-p_{f+Delta f}(x)|/|p_f(x)|. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Definition 2.1.)
exceptional_values: Definition 2.1 explicitly excludes p_n(x)=0 because the relative output denominator would vanish. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Definition 2.1.)
Distinctness of the x_j prevents zero denominators in the Lagrange basis products. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Section 2 opening paragraph and equation (2.1).)
higher_order_terms: The closed form and lower bound are exact; there is no omitted or big-O term. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Lemma 2.2, equation (2.2).)
hypotheses: The points x_j are pairwise distinct, and p_n is the polynomial of degree at most n interpolating f_j at x_j. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Section 2 opening paragraph.)
The evaluated exact value satisfies p_n(x) != 0. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Definition 2.1.)
Conditioning is with respect to variation of f only; x and all x_j remain fixed. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Section 2 opening paragraph.)
implicit_context: This is an exact conditioning result for the interpolation map f -> p_f(x), inherited from the setup immediately preceding Definition 2.1. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Section 2 opening paragraph through Definition 2.1.)
The result concerns one scalar output at one fixed x rather than the interpolating polynomial in a function norm. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Definition 2.1 and Lemma 2.2.)
norms: Only scalar absolute values and componentwise vector inequalities are used; no vector norm is specified. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Section 2 opening paragraph and Definition 2.1.)
numerical_model: No floating-point rounding model, precision parameter, or unit roundoff occurs in this result; epsilon is the relative input-perturbation radius. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Definition 2.1.)

undebatable_constraints: The numerator is a sum of termwise absolute values |ell_j(x)f_j|, not the absolute value of a different aggregate. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: equation (2.2).)
The denominator is the absolute value of the exact interpolant p_n(x), which must be nonzero. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Definition 2.1 and equation (2.2).)
All n+1 indices j=0,...,n are included. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: equations (2.1) and (2.2).)
The claim includes both the closed-form equality and the lower bound cond(x,n,f) >= 1. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Lemma 2.2, equation (2.2).)
Nodes and evaluation point are fixed; the conditioned input is f. (PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, anchor: Section 2 opening paragraph.)
